overview: The City Council ordained a new municipal budget process ordinance, approved a CPA appropriation for Thomas Brooks Park, and endorsed state PILOT legislation for tax-exempt institutions. Councilors also acted on business permits, discussed home rule petition and committee procedures, and addressed public concerns regarding peaceful demonstrations at Tufts University.

items.title: Commendations and Accolades
items.summary: Approved resolutions congratulating Brooks Elementary CCSR students for providing postal carrier safety whistles, honoring former Councilor Rick Caraviello as Chamber of Commerce Citizen of the Year, and commending the Medford High and Middle School music ensembles.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the records of the April 16, 2024 meeting as corrected.

items.title: Committee Reports
items.summary: Accepted reports from the Committee of the Whole on the preliminary budget, Planning and Permitting, Public Works and Facilities, and Resident Services and Public Engagement.

items.title: Special Permit: Snappy Patties (454 High Street)
items.summary: Approved a special permit to extend operating hours to 1:00 AM on Thursday through Saturday, subject to 30- and 60-day reviews by the building department.

items.title: Special Permit: Pinky's Famous Pizza (165 Main Street)
items.summary: Continued a public hearing on an extended operating hours petition to May 14, 2024, to allow the owner to coordinate with neighbors and city inspectors.

items.title: Annual Surveillance Report
items.summary: Tabled Paper 24-074 to May 14, 2024, to ensure missing introductory summary pages are included in the agenda packet.

items.title: Resolution Supporting State PILOT Legislation
items.summary: Approved Paper 24-093 in support of state bills S. 1836 and H. 2963, which would enable municipalities to require payments in lieu of taxes from large tax-exempt institutions.

items.title: CPA Appropriation: Thomas Brooks Park Phase II
items.summary: Approved a Community Preservation Committee appropriation of $287,500 from the CPA General Reserve for Phase II restoration work at Thomas Brooks Park.

items.title: Resolution on Subcommittee Processes
items.summary: Debated and defeated a resolution to examine committee procedures and request legal opinions concerning city council newsletters and the use of official titles in policy advocacy letters.

items.title: Firehouse Walking Tour
items.summary: Withdrew a resolution scheduling a walking tour of city firehouses after councilors confirmed an upcoming tour date.

items.title: Discussion on Home Rule Petitions Process
items.summary: Discussed the formal process and requirements for enacting home rule petitions, hearing public comment on affordable housing and real estate transfer taxes before placing the paper on file.

items.title: Hormel Stadium Food Truck Permits
items.summary: Approved food truck permits for various vendors scheduled at Hormel Stadium events.

items.title: Budget Ordinance
items.summary: Approved for third reading and ordained Paper 22-494, establishing a formal collaborative annual budget process between the City Council and the administration.

items.title: Personnel Ordinance Amendment: Supervisor of Water and Sewer
items.summary: Waived the three readings and ordained an amendment to the personnel ordinance reclassifying the supervisor of water and sewer position from PW-18 to PW-19.

items.title: Public Participation: Demonstrations at Tufts University
items.summary: Heard concerns regarding potential police response to peaceful student encampments at Tufts University, with several councilors expressing opposition to using municipal resources to clear the demonstrations.
